Unfortunately, the money doesn't matter to your average LEO. If a LEO loses a case of misconduct (which is rare), they aren't paying the costs out of their pension or their own pocket. The money ends up coming from the taxpayers.

Now, a system where the police pay with pension money isn't ideal by any means but it would certainly change how the police.. well.. police themselves. I honestly don't think there is a clear solution to their problem of police misconduct in America at the moment. Most solutions are either too aggressive or not aggressive enough. It would be nice if laws were enacted to hold LEOs to a higher standard, which I believe they should be, but the problem is that there is so much anti-cop hatred that the system would then be open to abuse by criminals or people who want to see the police fail. If the system were then abused, people would be scared to become police officers. If we lacked police officers, there is an almost certain chance crime would rise because criminals would realize they have the upper hand. It doesn't take a genius to see that any legal misstep can result in the entire system being destroyed. This statement can go both ways.

I don't want to take either side here but I can see the legitimate concerns from both LEO and non-LEO. It's a complicated situation.

I made a comment on eddit that the solution is to make police carry their own liability insurance or at least be responsible for a portion of the insurance. If every month they have to pay 50 to 100 dollars then they will start taking it seriously when the rates go up. Doctors, lawyers, electricians, roofers, etc all need liability insurance, why not police? It is a fair compromise. You don't take their pensions, but you do make them aware of the monetary issue.

The added bonus is things like vest cams and other recording devices will be a way to decrease their risk. There will be no false claims when there is a record.

Does anyone take a pre workout supplement before weight training? I've been thinking about trying one but I have some questions because they cost so much vs the amount of powder you get. Is there a particular brand you like? Is there more to it than just a lot of caffeine? Thank you all in advance!

• Water.
  • Caffeine does improve performance by very very little, and the more you use it, the less effective it is, so if you drink coffee you'll have to drop it. I don't think it's worth it.
  • I used to consume a supplement that peaks insulin; made me feel more alert. I found out (at least from my perception) I can get a similar effect just by ingesting sugary beverages; either way, the effect lasts only 30 minutes or so. Probably doesn't even affects performance.
  • Some carbs might be good if you haven't eaten in a while, and are used to eating at that time. Half a banana should do the trick.
  • Some protein is good to stimulate protein synthesis, but it's not like the difference is an order of magnitude. 10g BCAA with at least 4g of leucine is more than enough. Some people like adding more protein to their drinks as a mean to get more protein in their diet, but the only benefit is is to reach their daily target.
  • Creatine is best consumed after the workout.

Note that by no means you need a pre-workout supplement, and in my experience the best you can do is just eat some protein, carbs, and drink a bit of water. If money is a concern, you'll be better off spending that money in something else.
